definitions.explanation: The flat, green part of a plant. A casual/childish variant of 葉 (は).

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{葉|は}っぱで{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing with leaves.

examples.japanese: {緑|みどり}の{葉|は}っぱがきれいだ。
{秋|あき}になると{葉|は}っぱが{赤|あか}くなる。
examples.english: The leaves turn red in autumn.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{公園|こうえん}で{葉|は}っぱを{集|あつ}めて{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing by collecting leaves in the park.

notes:
{葉|は}っぱ is a casual/colloquial variant of {葉|は} (leaf). The っぱ suffix creates a friendly, informal tone.

REGISTER COMPARISON:
- {葉|は}っぱ: casual, childlike, conversational
- {葉|は}: standard, neutral, written

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {葉|は}っぱが{落|お}ちる: leaves fall
- {葉|は}っぱを{集|あつ}める: to collect leaves
- {葉|は}っぱで{遊|あそ}ぶ: to play with leaves

RELATED WORDS:
- {落|お}ち{葉|ば}: fallen leaves
- {青葉|あおば}: green leaves (fresh spring/summer foliage)
- {紅葉|もみじ}/{紅葉|こうよう}: autumn leaves, fall foliage
- {枯|か}れ{葉|は}: dead/withered leaves

NOTE:
{葉|は}っぱ is commonly used when speaking to or around children, but adults use it casually too.
